prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by small molecules that bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a new way of using a small molecule: instead of occupying an active site, a designed bifunctional molecule induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a target and the cell does the destruction. This meets my own test of a game-changer, because the idea is new and its consequences are already visible, with many degraders in clinical trials and a quantitative chemical framework (ligand design, ternary-complex cooperativity, linker optimisation) that is confirmed in many laboratories. It is also the one shortlisted candidate that all eight of us ranked, five of us in the top three, which is a more reliable signal than any single first place. The attribution core is reasonably clean: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated the PROTAC concept in 2001, and Ciulli supplied the structure-guided VHL recruiters and the ternary-complex mechanism that made the concept a design discipline. I have moved this to first place from third in my opening ballot, because after reading the colleagues' ballots I think it has the broadest and most robust support. My Car-Parrinello ballot (B037) is the cleaner prize on attribution and maturity, but no other member ranked it, and I do not regard it as a prize I can carry on my own advocacy.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity and attribution together. Clinical validation is still accumulating and, to my knowledge, no degrader is yet an approved drug, so a prize now risks running ahead of the consequences we usually want to see. The credited list has eight names, and a three-person cut leaves out the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito and the cereblon mechanism, with Gray and others), which is arguably the part with the strongest clinical footprint through thalidomide analogues. If the committee decides that the glue mechanism is inseparable from the prize, the Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli trio is not defensible, and the right answer may be to wait or to choose a candidate with a cleaner priority story.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing (B061) first for Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, and in his PROTAC ballot swaps Ciulli for Handa, arguing that the cereblon discovery explains molecular glues and that five or more credible names make a three-person cut unresolved.
responses.response: I accept the attribution difficulty and think his Handa point is the most serious objection to my trio. But the cereblon work explains why existing drugs work, while the PROTAC line of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli created a designable modality; those are two different achievements, and a prize citation can be written around induced proximity by design without pretending to cover every degrader. On base editing, I agree that it is elegant and fast moving, but I am not persuaded that giving a chemistry prize to two former trainees alongside Liu is how this committee would want to handle it, and I remain concerned about proximity to the 2020 genome-editing prize. I would rather hear from him whether he sees Handa as essential or only as an alternative third name.

responses.point: Brzezinski places long-range electron transfer through proteins (B055, Gray and Winkler) first, as a mature, physically well-understood mechanism underlying respiration and photosynthesis, and ranks degradation seventh as somewhat premature.
responses.response: I share his instinct for mature work with quantitative theory and experiment, and I take his maturity point against PROTACs seriously; it is my own main reservation. However, B055 received no support beyond his own ballot, and the foundational Marcus theory is already honoured, so the new element is the experimental protein programme and, as he himself says, the credit for that is narrower than the biology it supports. I would want him to state concretely what in the Gray work is new in chemical terms compared with the 1992 prize. I would keep it as a reference point for the standard of maturity but do not think it can compete on breadth of support.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B008, Buchwald and Hartwig) first as an enormously used, mature reaction with a clean two-person attribution, and says Kosugi's tin-amide work is a precursor, not the general method.
responses.response: I agree with him on the attribution: Kosugi was a stoichiometric-in-tin precursor, and Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, ligand-controlled method, so this is as clean as it gets. I ranked it sixth because the 2010 cross-coupling prize already established the principle of palladium-catalysed bond formation and I ask whether C-N coupling is a new idea or an extension of an honoured one. Zou argues that the 2010 prize did not cover amination, which is true, but it does weaken the novelty part of my game-changer test. I would keep it as a strong, safe candidate for a future year, but my view is that it has less conceptual novelty than degradation.

responses.point: Aili ranks degradation first as a programmable tool that removes a target protein rather than inhibiting it, and states that approved drugs are few but recognition is timely and the molecular glue strand is hard to fit into three names.
responses.response: I agree with the scientific framing and with his admission that credit is hard to split. Where I would qualify his position is the word timely. Timeliness is a judgment about the clinical record, and the committee should not be satisfied that mechanism confirmation alone justifies it. I would ask him whether he would support the prize if a specific degrader approval were still some years off, and whether he would rank the glue strand separately rather than adding Handa to the PROTAC trio.

responses.point: Zou prefers a Liu-only prize for base editing because the 2020 CRISPR prize makes a single-laureate award cleaner and credit for the trainees is uncertain, and ranks degradation third as conceptually original but possibly slightly early.
responses.response: I made the same Liu-only proposal in my opening ballot, and I still think it is the cleanest base-editing configuration. The difficulty I see after reading the others is that four colleagues propose Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, so there is no agreement on attribution within the group that supports B061 most strongly. Her slightly early verdict on degradation is also my own, so I think we agree that the real question for the committee is how much weight early clinical results should carry, and I do not think we have yet settled that.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that clinical validation of degraders is sufficient for a prize now, given that no approved PROTAC drug is established to my knowledge.
Whether the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) must be credited, which would change the trio or require splitting the achievement into two parts.
Whether base editing (B061) is judged too close to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether Liu alone or Liu with Komor and Gaudelli is the right attribution.
Whether my own Car-Parrinello candidate (B037) can attract any support beyond my ballot, since it is the cleanest case on priority and maturity.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. My postdoc with Arieh Warshel and my work on simulation of enzymes and ligand binding make me close to the computational field of B037 and to protein-folding theory (B001), but I have no direct collaboration with the named candidates, and I do not think this requires recusal.
